title: Rigorous bound on the aspect ratio for the formation of a nematic phase in hard rod and hard rectangle systems on $\mathbb{Z}^2$
abstract: We prove the existence of a nematic phase in a model of $l\times w$ hard rectangles on the square lattice with two allowed orientations and a large aspect ratio $k:=l/w$. The proof is based on a two-scale cluster expansion method developed previously by Disertori--Giuliani for hard rods in 2D and Disertori--Giuliani--Jauslin for hard plates in 3D. Our main contributions lie in explicitly tracking the constants and parameters and completing the arguments left implicit in these works. Hence, the proof produces a sufficient set of quantitative conditions from which estimates for the required aspect ratio can be extracted. A non-optimized evaluation of these conditions yields the bound $k\ge 10^{72}$. Although it vastly overshoots the numerical prediction, $k_{\min}=7$, our result appears to be the first rigorous estimate of the aspect ratio required for the formation of a nematic phase in hard rectangle systems.
summary: This paper provides a mathematically rigorous proof for the existence of a nematic phase in hard rectangle systems on a lattice by establishing a lower bound on the required aspect ratio ($k=l/w$). It achieves this using sophisticated cluster expansion methods and correlation function analysis, offering a significant theoretical advance despite yielding an overly conservative numerical estimate.
main_problem: The primary goal is to derive a rigorous, quantitative bound on the aspect ratio ($k=l/w$) required for hard rod and hard rectangle systems on the 2D lattice ($\mathbb{Z}^2$) to exhibit a nematic phase.
main_result: The authors provide a proof establishing the existence of a nematic phase for sufficiently large aspect ratios, yielding a rigorous lower bound (e.g., $k \ge 10^{72}$), although this vastly overshoots numerical estimates ($k_{\min}=7$).
method: The proof employs advanced mathematical techniques including two-scale cluster expansion methods, contour integration reminiscent of Pirogov–Sinai theory, and rigorous bounding of correlation functions.

main_assumptions: The rigorous bounds are contingent upon satisfying a large set of technical convergence and closure conditions derived from cluster expansion theory (e.g., C1 through C20).

paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the mathematical framework using cluster expansions for polymer partition functions. It then applies this machinery to derive bounds on correlation functions that diagnose symmetry breaking, culminating in a complex set of conditions whose satisfaction yields the final aspect ratio bound.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics models (hard shapes), the rigorous bounding techniques and use of advanced cluster expansions are highly relevant to understanding phase transitions in quantum many-body systems where mean-field approximations fail.
